tasks.short: Compile, administer and grade mathematical examinations

steps.what: Compile examination questions, marking keys and proof-assessment criteria
Administer the examination and handle student or delivery exceptions
Grade mathematical reasoning and check each final examination result

tasks.design: Configure fixed-key closed-question marking in {LMS}. Keep exam design, administration, proof assessment and final grade checks with the teacher; there is no automatic marking of mathematical reasoning or publication of final grades.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manually checking closed answers repeats an explicit key.
tasks.enabler_now: Native closed-question marking can apply that key consistently.
tasks.still_hard: A correct numerical answer can conceal invalid reasoning, and a valid proof can differ from an example.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognises mathematical validity, partial understanding and an ambiguous question.
tasks.altitude: Less closed-item checking, with examiner decisions unchanged.

reach.task: Test a closed-question key before release
reach.learn: Item versions and exam exception handling

evidence.claim: Ans automatically marks closed questions and supports open-answer marking workflows; this does not establish automated proof grading.
The examination shares and savings scenario are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is examination preparation through approved marks, excluding student-record publication and class-assignment grading.

In s1 the teacher produces item ID/version, accepted closed answers, point weights and exception rules, retaining all 30 hours including key capture and tests. In s2 the teacher obtains identified student submissions and resolves delivery issues, retaining all 25 hours. Missing keys or unmatched submissions are marked manually.
Use native fixed-choice or exact-key questions first; algebraic equivalence, symbolic proofs and uncertain answers go to human marking. No free structured proof-validity flag is assumed.
Allow four focal hours for key maintenance and exceptional response review beyond routine final checks.
unknowns: Closed-item share and current marking support
research_questions: Do key tests cover ambiguous closed answers while keeping all reasoning questions with the teacher?

already_counted.description: Open-answer assessment and final result checking

approvals.approved_version: Exact exam version, student submission, item marks and final result; changes require another teacher check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R85 gross15 minus4 upkeep =11 net. High requires a material manually marked closed-item share; low covers proof-only or already-auto-marked exams. Administration and proof marking retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Evaluate mathematical assignments and provide feedback

steps.what: Evaluate students' class work and record mathematical feedback decisions
Write feedback explaining the teacher's assessment and identified reasoning gaps

loop.purpose: Draft explanatory feedback from teacher decisions
loop.input: Teacher notes with exact assignment passages or equation references
loop.output: Draft feedback preserving the teacher's assessment without inventing mathematical corrections
loop.check: Teacher verifies every mathematical statement and example against the submission and intended feedback; remove unsupported deductions
loop.stop: One draft; an unsupported correction or unclear notation returns to manual feedback
loop.why_not_simpler: Test reusable comments first; individual explanations require varied wording

steps.what: Check feedback and approve the assignment mark and response

tasks.design: Draft feedback in {LMS} from the teacher's already-made mathematical assessment. Keep proof evaluation, mark selection and checking of every mathematical explanation with the teacher; the loop does not propose a grade.
tasks.previous_blocker: Explaining assessed reasoning gaps can require repetitive wording.
tasks.enabler_now: Feedback drafting from instructor notes is available, with human checking.
tasks.still_hard: A fluent explanation can contain invalid mathematics or misrepresent the student's reasoning.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher judges mathematical validity and chooses the most useful explanation.
tasks.altitude: Less feedback wording, with grading authority unchanged.

reach.task: Discuss recurring reasoning gaps using checked feedback examples

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes; this supports drafting, not validated mathematical reasoning or grade decisions.
The mathematics-feedback adaptation and time estimate are E1 model knowledge.

assumptions: Boundary is class-assignment assessment and feedback, excluding examinations and separate student-record transfer.

In s1 the teacher produces student/submission ID, rubric criterion, passage or equation reference, assessed issue, intended explanation and provisional mark. All 45 hours remain, including note capture. Missing source support requires manual feedback.
Test native comment banks before a loop. No structured proof-validity or automated mark is assumed.
Allow four focal hours for comment-template repair and failure review beyond routine feedback checks.
research_questions: Does drafting reduce net feedback time without adding mathematical errors or changing teacher assessment?

already_counted.description: Mathematical assessment and final feedback check

approvals.approved_version: Exact student submission, assignment mark and checked feedback version; changes require another teacher check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R88 gross12 minus4 upkeep =8 net. High assumes individual feedback wording; low covers proof-heavy corrections or effective existing comment banks. Evaluation time remains.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver mathematical science lectures

steps.what: Select lecture explanations, examples and mathematical derivations
Lay out lecture slides and handouts from the selected material
Check notation and deliver lectures with student questions and worked explanations

tasks.design: Configure a mathematical presentation template in {DOCS} to place exact teacher-selected content. Keep content design, notation checking and live lecture delivery with the teacher; the template does not generate proofs or choose examples.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated slide placement can consume time after content has been prepared.
tasks.enabler_now: Native templates can reuse a fixed layout without a model.
tasks.still_hard: Line breaks, symbols and omitted assumptions can alter mathematical meaning.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher explains reasoning and responds to student misconceptions in real time.
tasks.altitude: Less formatting, with teaching and mathematical responsibility unchanged.

reach.task: Check readability of mathematical teaching materials

evidence.claim: Exact-content lecture layout is an E1 design from model knowledge; no digest source validates automatic mathematical lecture creation.

assumptions: Boundary is lecture preparation and delivery, not curriculum design or student grading.

The teacher produces title, ordered text, equations, diagram assets, captions and layout choices in s1, retaining all 45 hours including capture. Unsupported notation or overflow returns to manual layout, never silent truncation.
Test native slide templates first; only repetitive placement loses time.
Allow four focal hours for template and notation-layout exceptions beyond routine teaching checks.
unknowns: Current formatting burden and notation formats
research_questions: Does the template preserve equation meaning and readability in long derivations?

already_counted.description: Content preparation, notation check and live delivery

approvals.approved_version: Exact lecture file, equations, diagrams and handouts checked before delivery; changed content requires another teacher check

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R80 gross20 minus4 upkeep =16 net for repeated manual layout. Low covers already-templated materials or complex notation fallback. Content and live delivery retain time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Maintain attendance, grades and required student records

steps.what: Capture attendance and select approved grades for the required student records
Transfer required attendance and grade fields into the second student-record system
Check staged student records and confirm their publication

tasks.design: Configure a staged transfer from {LMS} to the student-record system {OTHER} where a second entry is required. The teacher captures attendance, selects already-approved results and checks the exact destination records before confirming publication; grades are not recalculated.
tasks.previous_blocker: Separate learning and student-record systems can require repeated entry.
tasks.enabler_now: Native export and import can reuse checked fields.
tasks.still_hard: Student identity, assessment versions and corrected marks need careful reconciliation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognises when a record does not match the approved assessment.
tasks.altitude: Less duplicate entry, with record capture and final checks unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve a mismatched student or assessment record

evidence.claim: Radboud requires grades to be published in both Brightspace and OSIRIS, documenting a dual-publication requirement rather than a measured saving.
Staged transfer and the time estimate are E1 model knowledge and depend on a real duplicate-entry baseline.

assumptions: Boundary is record maintenance, not choosing marks in the separate exam and assignment tasks.

In s1 the teacher produces student ID, course/assessment ID, result version, approved mark, attendance date/status and correction indicator. All 50 hours remain for observation, capture and selection. Missing mappings require manual entry and checks.
The second student-record system is {OTHER}. Test native export/import first; existing sync runtime earns no saving. No free structured attendance status is assumed.
Allow four focal hours for mapping and transfer exceptions beyond routine confirmation; no new student-administration curation is transferred.
unknowns: Available identifiers and native transfer support
research_questions: Can staged transfers reconcile exact approved results and corrected marks without publishing prematurely?

already_counted.description: Attendance capture, result selection and publication check

approvals.approved_version: Exact destination record set, student and assessment IDs, result versions, marks and attendance fields; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R70 gross30 minus4 upkeep =26 net. High requires manual second-system entry; low covers existing sync. Attendance capture, mark decisions and final checks are not removed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce fixed-key marking, feedback wording, lecture layout and duplicate record entry while preserving mathematical assessment and teaching.
role.ambitious_version: A mathematics teacher who spends less time repeating checked content and more time explaining and assessing reasoning.
